from.place: Proof, second paragraph: "After an algebraically closed extension"; the separating-basis fact verifies that such extensions satisfy the separable hypothesis of the algebraic normalization comparison.

title: A finitely generated extension of an algebraically closed field has a separating basis
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field] (every nonconstant polynomial over $k$ has a root in $k$) and $L/k$ a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] generated as a field by finitely many elements. There are finitely many elements $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in L$ forming a transcendence basis of $L/k$ [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis], such that $L/k(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$ is separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. The empty basis is allowed.

source.place: Tag 030Z (lemma-perfect), together with Definition 030O (definition-separable-field-extension): algebraically closed fields have pth roots and hence are perfect; finite generation specializes separability to a separating basis.
